questions.explain: The practical baseline is 512-token chunks with 50-token overlap so semantic content is never split across chunk boundaries; feeding a 200-page PDF as one string is not an option.
options: One embedding per entire document regardless of length
50-token chunks with 512-token overlap
Chunking is unnecessary — models accept unlimited input
512-token chunks with 50-token overlap, because text-embedding-3-small supports 8,191 tokens while sentence-transformer models typically support 512

questions.explain: CLIP's contrastive training projects images and text into a shared space; CLIP ViT-L/14 (768 dims) is the standard starting point for production image search.
options: It embeds images and text into the same vector space, enabling cross-modal queries — you can retrieve images using a text string as the query
It produces 2,048-dimensional vectors, the largest available
It only works with Euclidean distance
It eliminates the need for any database

questions.explain: Audio arrives at different sample rates and codecs; enforce the normalization step the way you would enforce data type coercion in an ETL pipeline.
options: It accepts any sample rate and codec without preprocessing
It requires stereo MP3 at 44.1 kHz only

It requires 16 kHz mono PCM, so build a normalization step (librosa resample / ffmpeg) at the front of the ingestion pipeline — feeding 8 kHz telephone audio without upsampling degrades embedding quality
It requires video input, not audio

questions.explain: File-level embedding loses too much precision; the practical standard is function/class-level units including docstring, signature, and body.
options: Embed each entire repository as one vector
File-level embedding is too coarse; use function-level or class-level chunking — parse the AST (Python's ast module, or tree-sitter for multi-language codebases) and embed each function/method/class
Chunk by line count only, ignoring structure
Code cannot be embedded; use regex search instead
